# Trademark Policy

Relaticle Inc owns the Relaticle name and logo (the "Marks"). The [AGPL-3.0 license](../LICENSE) governs the code. This policy governs the Marks. It takes away none of the rights the license gives you over the code.

The goal is simple: when someone sees the Relaticle name, they should be able to trust it means software and services from us.

## You may, without asking

- Self-host Relaticle for your own organization and call it Relaticle, including on your own subdomain such as `crm.example.com`.
- Refer to Relaticle truthfully in articles, reviews, tutorials, talks, and comparisons.
- Say your product or service works with Relaticle, for example "Sync for Relaticle" or "integrates with Relaticle", as long as nothing suggests we made or endorse it.
- Link to relaticle.com or to the official repository.
- Keep the name in the code. Namespaces, package names, and class names that contain "Relaticle" do not need to change.

## You need our written permission to

- Offer Relaticle to other people or organizations as a hosted, managed, or resold service under the Relaticle name or logo.
- Distribute a modified version of Relaticle under the Relaticle name or logo.
- Use the Marks, or anything confusingly similar to them, in a company name, product name, domain name, app store listing, or social media handle.
- Use the Marks in advertising, including paid search keywords.
- Sell merchandise that carries the Marks.
- Register the Marks, or anything confusingly similar to them, as a trademark, domain name, or business name.

## If you host or fork Relaticle for others

The license lets you do this. The Marks are what you leave behind:

1. Choose your own name and logo, and remove ours from the interface, the marketing pages, and outgoing emails.
2. Do not copy relaticle.com marketing copy, screenshots, or pricing pages.
3. You may state the origin factually, for example: "Based on Relaticle, an open source CRM. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Relaticle Inc."
4. Under section 13 of the AGPL-3.0, offer the source of your modified version to every user who interacts with it over a network.
